report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to produce news/blog-style content — i.e., to adopt a web media/newsroom/blog domain (headlines, sections, and related site/UI tokens). In practice this means B is biased toward generating newsy headlines and blog-roll style continuations with politics/celebrity terms, section labels, and media/link widgets (Blog, Video, Photo, http, ads).

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly newsroom/blog domain:
  - People/roles typical of journalism: “politicians,” “journalists/journalist,” “activists,” “spokesman/spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “legislators,” “billionaire,” and frequent “Obama.”
  - Site/section/navigation and media widgets: “blogs,” “blogger,” “blogging,” “Blog,” “video,” “photo,” “TV,” “http,” “Mail,” “ads,” months (“Mar,” “May”), dashes and parentheses — all common on news/blog index pages and article headers.
  - Section-like terms: “metropolitan,” “Religious,” “Political/ political,” plus general headline-y vocabulary.
  - Social/clicky blog terms: “facebook,” “blogger,” “hottest,” “sexy,” suggesting blog/social-media flavored content.
- The difference is strongest at early token positions in higher layers (very large norms at layers 18–25, especially p1–p4), which is characteristic of a style/domain steering signal injected early in the sequence and consolidated late in the network.
- Tokens like “metropolitan,” “Obama,” “billionaire,” months, and media widgets repeatedly top the lists across layers/positions, indicating a consistent shift toward news/blog front-page/headline distributions rather than general web text.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a news/blog generation behavior — pushing the model toward newsroom/blog-roll style outputs (headlines, sections, media links, and related political/celebrity content).
